key_insight: AD-WM makes world models better at choosing actions, not just predicting next states. It learns a joint embedding that can tell candidate actions apart from the same starting state, which is exactly what counterfactual MPC needs.
problem_solved: Standard latent world models are optimized for factual next-step prediction, so they may look accurate while still failing to distinguish which action is best. This paper addresses the mismatch between prediction training and action comparison in model predictive control.
method: Uses a joint-embedding world model designed for action discrimination in counterfactual settings.
Combines residual latent dynamics with predictor-level action-recovery regularization.
Leverages inverse dynamics and normalized representation learning to better separate alternative actions from the same state.
impact: For practitioners, this means better planning reliability in settings where multiple actions must be compared from one state. It can improve MPC performance without relying solely on lower prediction error as the training objective.

paper_title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
paper_authors: Jiabin Qiu, Zixuan Chen, Hongye Cao, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo
